# About AsterByte Solutions

## Company profile

AsterByte Solutions is an Indian software consultancy and development firm. It helps startups and growing businesses turn operational problems into useful websites, applications, automation and AI tools.

Founded in 2019 by Divyanshu Dwivedi, an IIT graduate, AsterByte Solutions has worked with more than 50 clients and delivered more than 200 service engagements across development, consulting, integrations and ongoing improvements.

The company's ambition is to become a leading software consultancy through practical advice, dependable delivery and long-term client relationships.

## What the company does

- Websites and customer-facing web applications.
- Full-stack product development, including frontend, backend, APIs and databases.
- Business applications such as CRMs, appointment systems and internal dashboards.
- AI assistants, document search and AI features integrated into existing workflows.
- Process automation and connections between business tools.
- Cloud delivery, testing, maintenance and performance improvements.

The agency can deliver a complete product or contribute specialists to an existing team. The recommended approach depends on the customer's workflow, budget and technical constraints.

## How a project works

1. **Understand the problem.** Discuss users, current process, pain points and the outcome that matters.
2. **Define the first release.** Agree on essential features, assumptions, integrations and acceptance criteria.
3. **Prepare a proposal.** Provide scope, indicative schedule, commercial terms and responsibilities for review.
4. **Design and build.** Review designs and working demonstrations at agreed milestones.
5. **Test and accept.** Validate the agreed workflows and track defects before handover.
6. **Launch and hand over.** Supply custom project source code, setup instructions, agreed documentation and a walkthrough.
7. **Support and improve.** Fix qualifying development bugs free for the product's lifetime; quote enhancements separately when needed.

## Useful information for a new inquiry

Start with the business problem. Ask for missing details one at a time: primary users, important workflows, existing software, integrations, approximate budget, preferred launch date and who will approve the work. A caller can begin without a complete specification.

A requested date is a preference until delivery capacity and scope are reviewed. Do not collect passwords, payment-card details, OTPs or production database exports during a sales call.

## Working principles and policies

- Recommend the smallest useful solution before expanding the scope.
- Explain tradeoffs in everyday language and use AI where it has a clear purpose.
- Record scope and change requests so both parties understand cost and timing.
- Provide custom project source code after agreed payments are complete. Third-party components retain their own licenses.
- Keep customer records and private project material restricted to authorized people.
- Obtain permission before discussing a real client's identity, metrics or project details publicly.
- Do not promise specific business results, AI accuracy, regulatory certification or uninterrupted service without evidence and explicit agreement.

## Contact and consultations

Public support contact details are managed in the application configuration. Do not substitute the founder's personal contact details. Use the application's configured contact channel when one becomes available.

An introductory discovery discussion of up to 30 minutes is free as part of the introductory offer. Longer workshops or detailed audits may be paid. Consultation availability must come from a connected calendar or human confirmation; expertise alone does not imply a free slot.

See [services and pricing](services-pricing.md), [team expertise](team-expertise.md) and [support policies](support-policies.md).

# Services, indicative pricing and delivery

## Pricing basis

The following INR ranges help customers plan a focused first release. Each range assumes timely customer feedback and reusable standard components. The final proposal confirms the deliverables, acceptance criteria, dependencies and price.

| Service | Typical first-release scope | Indicative budget | Indicative build time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Landing page or small business website | Up to 5 pages, responsive design and inquiry form | INR 15,000-35,000 | 1-2 weeks |
| Business website with content management | Up to 12 pages, editable content and basic analytics integration | INR 35,000-75,000 | 2-4 weeks |
| Full-stack web MVP | Sign-in, 2-3 roles, up to 3 core workflows and an admin area | INR 80,000-2,00,000 | 4-8 weeks |
| Custom CRM or business application | Leads or operational records, permissions, tasks and standard reports | INR 70,000-1,80,000 | 4-8 weeks |
| Workflow automation | One defined workflow connecting up to 2 existing tools | INR 15,000-50,000 | 1-3 weeks |
| AI assistant or document-search pilot | One approved knowledge collection, one channel and basic evaluation | INR 35,000-1,00,000 | 2-5 weeks |
| Additional API integration | One documented API and one agreed workflow | INR 10,000-35,000 | 1-2 weeks |
| Dedicated full-stack developer | One developer for up to 160 working hours per month; capacity agreed in advance | INR 75,000-1,25,000/month | Availability confirmed separately |
| Technical consultation | Architecture, feasibility or workflow review | INR 1,000-2,000/hour | Scheduled separately |
| Optional maintenance | Up to 5 hours/month of monitoring, dependency review and small improvements | INR 5,000-12,000/month | Monthly plan |

Build time starts after scope approval, the agreed initial payment and required content/access are available. External approvals, customer review and integration dependencies can extend elapsed time. A combined project is scoped as a whole; do not blindly add table rows or offer the lowest price for every request. AI voice and provider charges are separate from development cost.

## What development includes

- Agreed design and implementation, responsive behavior where applicable, and testing of the agreed workflows.
- Custom frontend, backend and database migration source code relevant to the project.
- Setup instructions, configuration variable names, agreed documentation and one handover session of up to 60 minutes.
- One deployment to the agreed environment when hosting access is available.
- Revision rounds and post-launch refinements within the limits below.
- Lifetime correction of qualifying development bugs in the delivered scope.

Source code is handed over after agreed payments are complete. Client-specific custom code belongs to the client under the project terms; pre-existing reusable tools and third-party components retain their existing ownership and licenses. Credentials are transferred through an appropriate secure process, never committed into source code.

## Revisions and free updates

| Deliverable | Included revision rounds | Free post-launch refinement allowance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Websites | 2 consolidated rounds | Up to 6 development hours within 90 calendar days of handover |
| Business apps, MVPs and AI pilots | 3 consolidated rounds | Up to 12 development hours within 90 calendar days of handover |

A revision round is one consolidated list of feedback on an agreed milestone. It can cover layout, wording and behavior inside the approved scope. Unused rounds do not become a budget for new features. Free refinements cover small text, spacing, labels and comparable adjustments; the allowance is a total per project, not per request. It expires after 90 days and does not roll over.

Extra revisions or enhancements can be estimated at INR 800-1,500/hour or quoted as a fixed change request. Explain the estimate and obtain agreement before paid work starts. Bug fixes do not consume revision rounds or the refinement allowance.

## Faster delivery

An expedited schedule may be available for an additional 20-40% of the agreed development price. A delivery lead must first confirm staffing, dependencies and a revised schedule. An extra fee does not guarantee that every deadline is feasible. Testing and acceptance remain part of delivery.

## Lifetime development bug fixes

A qualifying bug is a reproducible defect in AsterByte Solutions' delivered custom code that fails the written acceptance criteria under the supported environment defined at handover. Examples include an agreed calculation giving the wrong result or a save action failing for valid input.

Correction of these development bugs is free for the lifetime of that delivered product, including after the 90-day refinement period and without an active maintenance subscription. There is no arbitrary cap on qualifying defects. The customer must provide enough information and appropriate access for diagnosis.

New features, changed requirements, customer or third-party code changes, new platform compatibility work, provider outages, expired subscriptions and infrastructure charges are outside this free-fix promise. If cause is uncertain, investigate before classifying it or requesting paid work. A regression introduced by AsterByte Solutions' own fix remains covered. Lifetime coverage promises free qualifying correction, not immediate or 24/7 staffing.

## Exclusions and payments

Domain names, hosting, paid assets, provider subscriptions, AI usage, messaging, payment-gateway charges and applicable taxes are outside the displayed estimates unless a proposal includes them. Paid maintenance adds proactive work; it is not required to access qualifying bug fixes.

The standard payment schedule is 40% at kickoff, 40% after the agreed working milestone and 20% before final handover. Smaller assignments may use a simpler schedule documented in the proposal. Cancellation is reviewed against delivered work and approved nonrecoverable costs; the agent must not invent a refund amount or approve a refund.

See [support policies](support-policies.md) for response targets and escalation. A signed project agreement takes precedence over these general estimates.

# Teams, expertise and consultation routing

AsterByte Solutions brings together specialists across five delivery teams. Anjali is the company's AI representative and routes consultations to the relevant human specialist.

## Five delivery teams

| Team | Specialists | Responsibilities and consultation topics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full-stack development and UI/UX | Meera Kapoor, frontend and UX lead; Arjun Verma, backend lead | Websites, web apps, accessible interfaces, user journeys, APIs, permissions and database design |
| Business solutions | Nikhil Rao, business systems consultant | CRMs, appointment workflows, internal tools, process mapping, reporting and requirements discovery |
| AI development | Sana Iqbal, AI engineer | Document search, RAG, assistants, model integration, evaluation and human review workflows |
| Automation and integrations | Kabir Sethi, integration engineer | Repetitive tasks, external APIs, webhooks, synchronization, retries and duplicate-action prevention |
| Cloud delivery and quality engineering | Priya Nair, cloud and QA lead; Ishaan Shah, support specialist | Deployment, CI/CD, backups, regression testing, incident triage, monitoring and performance investigation |

## Technology capabilities

- **Frontend and UX:** React, Next.js, TypeScript, HTML/CSS, responsive layouts, design prototypes and usability reviews.
- **Backend and data:** Node.js, Express, Python, FastAPI, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Supabase, MongoDB, Redis and SQLite where suitable.
- **AI:** Retrieval, embeddings, model APIs, tool calling, prompt design, evaluation sets and reviewable AI output.
- **Integrations:** Business APIs, webhooks, scheduled jobs and provider-supported connections. Compatibility is checked per project.
- **Delivery and QA:** Git, Docker, GitHub Actions, browser testing, API tests, deployment documentation and recovery planning.

The team selects technologies according to project requirements. Confirm compatibility and scope before committing to a particular integration or platform.

## Choosing the right consultation

- A new product with unclear requirements starts with Nikhil; bring Meera and Arjun in once the main workflows are understood.
- A website or user-experience problem starts with Meera. Authentication, database or API design questions go to Arjun.
- An AI assistant or document-answering requirement goes to Sana. Confirm the knowledge sources, acceptable failure behavior and evaluation plan.
- A manual process or connection between tools goes to Kabir. Ask what triggers the workflow and what should happen if a step fails.
- Deployment, reliability and testing questions go to Priya.
- Existing-product problems start with Ishaan, who routes the issue to the owning engineer. Suspected security incidents follow the urgent escalation policy immediately.

Do not promise a particular employee, start date or consultation slot until availability is confirmed. A team routing recommendation is not a booking.

## Authority and limits

Specialists can assess feasibility and estimate effort. The delivery lead confirms schedules and final scope. Commercial exceptions, refunds and binding commitments require an authorized human decision. The AI representative can collect requirements and explain this documentation; it cannot approve exceptions or claim engineering work has been completed.

See [case studies](case-studies.md) for project team assignments and [support policies](support-policies.md) for escalation.

# Client case studies

A selection of projects delivered by AsterByte Solutions across logistics, automation, marketing and developer tools.

## CS-001: DispatchPro - logistics operations

**Client:** SwiftRoute Logistics.

**Adoption:** 1,200 customer accounts, 30 couriers and 5 operations staff.

**Problem:** Delivery requests, courier assignments and status updates were scattered across manual processes. Customers needed clear quotes and tracking, while operations staff needed controlled status changes and exception handling.

**Solution:** A multi-role logistics application with zone and weight-based pricing, role-controlled order transitions, courier assignment, OTP delivery confirmation and failed-delivery recovery. A support assistant combines FAQ retrieval with role-scoped access to tracking and pricing information.

**Technologies:** React, Node.js, Express, MongoDB, transaction and concurrency controls, embeddings and MongoDB Atlas Vector Search.

**Team:** Arjun led backend workflows, Meera led the interface, Kabir handled integrations and Priya coordinated testing.

**Outcome:** Customers, couriers and administrators work from a shared delivery record, with consistent pricing logic and clear operational handoffs.

**Spoken summary:** "We built DispatchPro for SwiftRoute Logistics to bring delivery pricing, tracking and courier coordination into one application."

## CS-002: FormPilot - assisted form completion

**Client:** NextStep Career Services.

**Adoption:** 300 candidate profiles and 8 coordinators.

**Problem:** Candidates repeatedly entered the same information into placement and application forms. Personal questions still needed individual judgment and review.

**Solution:** A Chrome extension detects fields, matches them against a local profile and saved corrections, fills supported controls and checks the results. AI assistance supports unresolved field mapping and reviewable answer drafts. Users remain in control of personal answers and consent.

**Technologies:** Chrome Manifest V3, FastAPI, SQLite and Playwright.

**Team:** Kabir led form adapters, Sana handled assisted mapping and answer review, and Priya covered browser testing.

**Outcome:** Less repeated entry, reusable corrections and a clear review step for uncertain answers. Routine profile matching runs locally; AI-assisted parsing and drafting use the configured AI service.

**Spoken summary:** "FormPilot helps NextStep's candidates fill routine details from saved information while reviewing answers that need personal judgment."

## CS-003: Draftly - reviewable marketing content

**Client:** Blueframe Digital.

**Adoption:** 24 editors and reviewers across 6 brand workspaces.

**Problem:** The marketing team needed a repeatable process for turning briefs into content while checking brand rules and preserving editorial control.

**Solution:** A workflow coordinates research, writing, brand-policy checks and visual direction. Users inspect, edit, reject or retry drafts before publishing, with live progress throughout the process.

**Technologies:** Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, CrewAI, OpenRouter and server-sent events.

**Team:** Sana led AI workflow design, Meera handled the review interface and Arjun handled data and API integration.

**Outcome:** Consistent review steps, clearer handoffs and human approval before publication. Automated policy checks support editorial review rather than replacing it.

**Spoken summary:** "We built Draftly so Blueframe's team can research, draft and review content against its brand rules before publishing."

## CS-004: RepoLens - explainable repository review

**Client:** CodeBridge Learning.

**Adoption:** 180 learners and 12 mentors.

**Problem:** Mentors needed a repeatable way to review project documentation and engineering signals with explanations behind each recommendation.

**Solution:** A repository review application analyzes documentation, commits, technology choices and structure. It produces deterministic scores, supporting findings and a prioritized improvement roadmap. Optional Gemini assistance improves the wording of recommendations without deciding the score.

**Technologies:** Next.js, TypeScript, GitHub API, Zod, Recharts and Gemini.

**Team:** Arjun implemented analysis workflows, Meera designed the report interface and Priya reviewed validation and failure handling.

**Outcome:** Structured project feedback that mentors can explain and learners can act on. Repository scores provide engineering signals rather than a hiring or security certification.

**Spoken summary:** "RepoLens gives CodeBridge's mentors and learners an explained repository review with practical suggestions for improvement."

# ClinicFlow appointment system - support guide

## Product and scope

ClinicFlow is the appointment management system delivered by AsterByte Solutions for ClearCare Clinic. This guide covers reception workflows, doctor schedules, appointment status and common support checks.

The first release covers doctor availability, appointments, reception check-in, booking status and daily operational summaries. It is an administrative scheduling product, not a diagnosis tool, emergency service or complete electronic health-record system.

## Roles and features

- **Receptionist:** Search permitted patient contact records, create appointments, reschedule, cancel and check in visitors.
- **Doctor:** View their own schedule and update appointment completion status.
- **Clinic administrator:** Manage staff access, doctor hours, appointment durations and permitted reports.

Appointments use Scheduled, Checked in, Completed, Cancelled and No-show statuses. Cancelled appointments remain in history. Email or SMS reminders exist only if the relevant provider is configured; sending and delivery are separate outcomes.

The clinic uses India Standard Time, Asia/Kolkata. Confirm the date and time aloud when discussing a booking.

## Common workflows

### Create an appointment

1. An authorized receptionist searches for an existing contact before creating another record.
2. Open Appointments, choose New appointment, and select the doctor, date and an available slot.
3. Confirm the contact details and appointment reason using the minimum necessary information.
4. Save once and check for a confirmation and appointment reference.

Only say the appointment is booked after the operation actually succeeds. This guide cannot establish live slot availability.

### Reschedule or cancel

Open the appointment by its reference, check current status, select Reschedule or Cancel, confirm the intended change and save. Check the saved result before repeating. A failed notification does not prove that the appointment change failed.

### Check in and complete

Reception changes Scheduled to Checked in when the visitor arrives. The authorized doctor marks the appointment Completed. A mistaken status needs an authorized correction; do not delete the appointment to hide the history.

## Troubleshooting reference

Start with these diagnostic checks. Confirm the cause before marking an issue resolved, and escalate when the symptoms persist or the steps do not fit the affected version.

| Issue ID | Symptom | Checks and next step | Expected result / escalation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CLIN-001 | No slots appear | Check doctor, date, clinic timezone and active filters. Ask the clinic admin to review working hours and leave. | Slots appear if configuration was the cause. If valid hours still produce no slots, report the doctor/date and scope of impact. |
| CLIN-002 | A slot becomes unavailable during booking | Refresh availability and inspect whether another appointment already occupies it. Offer a different confirmed slot. | Avoid a double booking. If two confirmed appointments share one exclusive slot, escalate with both references. |
| CLIN-003 | Save seems stuck or a confirmation is missing | Check the appointment list for the reference before clicking Save again. Record the time and visible message. | Prevent duplicate creation. If state is uncertain, stop retries and contact support. |
| CLIN-004 | Reminder was not received | Confirm the saved appointment exists, contact details are correct and reminders are enabled. An authorized support engineer checks provider status. | Do not create another appointment. Escalate confirmed send failures with the appointment reference. |
| CLIN-005 | An appointment looks missing | Check doctor, date, status filters, timezone and role permissions. Search by appointment reference. | If absent with correct access and filters, report possible missing data; do not recreate or delete records blindly. |
| CLIN-006 | Access denied | Check the signed-in account and ask the clinic admin to review assigned access. | Legitimate permissions are restored by an authorized admin. Never bypass the role check or share another person's login. |

## Known limitations and escalation

The first release supports one clinic location, configurable doctor schedules and basic reports. It excludes insurance claims, prescriptions, clinical decisions, offline synchronization and external hospital integrations unless separately scoped. Do not claim a health-data compliance certification.

Collect the appointment reference, affected role, approximate time, visible error and whether the issue affects one person or the clinic. Avoid patient medical details in a general support conversation. Screenshots should redact unrelated names and contact information.

Clinic-wide booking failure may be P1 under [support policies](support-policies.md). A single-user issue with a workaround is usually P2. Suspected record exposure or loss is P1. Technical support must not advise on medical emergencies; direct those to the clinic's established emergency procedure.

# LeadBridge CRM - support guide

## Product and scope

LeadBridge is the CRM delivered by AsterByte Solutions for BrightPath Services. It tracks inquiries, ownership, follow-ups and sales stages. This guide explains the main workflows and support checks.

## Roles and workflows

- **Sales representative:** Works on assigned leads, records activity and manages follow-up tasks.
- **Sales manager:** Assigns leads, reviews team pipeline and resolves ownership issues.
- **Administrator:** Manages roles, imports, integrations and permitted exports.

The default pipeline is New, Contacted, Qualified, Proposal sent, Negotiation, Won and Lost. A stage describes sales progress; it does not prove an invoice was paid or a contract signed. Store an amount and expected closing date only when provided or confirmed.

### Add and qualify a lead

1. Search by contact or company before creating a record.
2. Select Leads, then New lead. Enter name, company, contact channel and inquiry summary.
3. Set an owner and record the source. Collect only the information needed for follow-up.
4. Save and verify the returned lead reference.
5. Add requirements, approximate budget, preferred timeline and a next action as they become known.

### Follow up and update stages

Open the lead, add a note describing the conversation, and create a task with an owner and due date. Use Asia/Kolkata for the team's local dates. A completed call and a completed follow-up task are different records.

Move a lead only when the stage's event happened. Mark Proposal sent after actual sending is confirmed. Mark Won after the authorized team confirms acceptance. Record a Lost reason without erasing the lead's history.

### Imports and duplicate review

An authorized admin maps CSV columns, previews validation results and reviews likely duplicate contacts before confirming the import. Email or phone similarity is a review signal, not proof two people are the same. Merge only through an authorized workflow that preserves history; the agent cannot merge records from a caller's request alone.

### Reports

Pipeline value reflects entered deal amounts in the selected stages. Closed-won value is not automatically recognized revenue. Filters, owner access, time ranges and timezone can change the report. Exports require explicit permission.

## Troubleshooting reference

Use these checks to narrow down the issue. Record the outcome before deciding whether a fix or engineering escalation is needed.

| Issue ID | Symptom | Checks and next step | Expected result / escalation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CRM-001 | A lead is missing | Check search text, owner, stage and date filters. Confirm the signed-in user's access; search by reference if available. | Restore visibility if a filter was responsible. Escalate an authorized missing record with its reference. |
| CRM-002 | A save fails | Review validation errors and required fields. Confirm permitted access and connection, then inspect whether the record already saved before retrying. | A valid change saves once. Stop on uncertain status to avoid duplicates. |
| CRM-003 | A lead appears twice | Compare references and activity history. Ask a manager to review duplicate status. | Preserve both histories until an authorized merge is completed. Do not delete either record as a first response. |
| CRM-004 | A follow-up is overdue or absent | Check task owner, due date, timezone, completion state and filters. | Correct task visibility or scheduling. Reminder delivery needs separate provider evidence. |
| CRM-005 | Pipeline totals look wrong | Check stages, date basis, owner filters, currency and empty or duplicate deal amounts. | Explain the report inputs. Persistent calculation mismatches go to engineering with a redacted example. |
| CRM-006 | CSV import reports rejected rows | Review required column mappings and the row validation report. Correct a small sample and preview again. | Only valid, reviewed rows proceed. Do not repeatedly import the full file or overwrite records blindly. |
| CRM-007 | Email is not received | Confirm whether the send operation was accepted, then have support check delivery status and configured sender details. | Distinguish saved activity, accepted send and actual delivery. Avoid duplicate sends while state is uncertain. |

## Limitations and support handoff

LeadBridge supports one organization and INR deal amounts in its current release. Accounting, payroll, billing, marketing campaigns, automatic prospect scraping and offline editing are outside the first release. Integrations are available only when separately implemented and configured. The CRM does not guarantee sales outcomes.

Before retrieving private data, verify the caller's identity and organization/project access through the application. A supplied email, phone number or lead reference is only a lookup hint.

For escalation, capture the lead/task reference, affected role, timestamp, exact visible message, recent action and whether others are affected. Keep client lists and full CSV exports out of public knowledge. Organization-wide inability to save or suspected data exposure is P1; a limited issue with a workaround is normally P2. See [support policies](support-policies.md).

# Support, priorities and escalation

## Coverage and hours

These support terms cover projects delivered by AsterByte Solutions. A project-specific agreement takes precedence where it defines different coverage or response commitments.

Standard staffed hours are Monday-Friday, 10:00-19:00 India Standard Time, Asia/Kolkata, excluding company holidays. One business day means 9 staffed hours. There is no default 24/7 response commitment. Out-of-hours coverage requires a separately agreed arrangement.

The voice agent may collect an issue outside staffed hours only when the calling service is operational. Intake does not imply an engineer is currently available. No support email, holiday calendar, public phone number or emergency contact is configured by these documents; do not invent one.

## Priority and response targets

Response means a human acknowledges the issue and begins triage. It does not mean the problem is resolved. Targets count staffed hours from successful ticket submission, with the clock beginning at the next staffed period for an out-of-hours submission.

| Priority | Impact | Initial human response target | Update target while actively investigated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 - Critical | Production service unavailable for most users; core workflow blocked without a workaround; suspected data exposure or loss | Within 2 business hours | Every 4 business hours or sooner on a material change |
| P2 - High | Important function degraded for a subset of users, or a workable alternative exists | Within 1 business day | Each business day |
| P3 - Normal | Isolated noncritical defect, cosmetic issue or ordinary product question | Within 2 business days | Every 3 business days while open |
| P4 - Enhancement | New feature, improvement or change of scope | Within 3 business days | Schedule agreed after scoping |

Support may reclassify priority after reviewing impact and will explain why. Contract-specific terms take precedence. Resolution time depends on cause, reproducibility, access and external dependencies; do not promise a fix by the response deadline.

## Intake and record creation

Collect the product or project, brief symptom, time first observed, affected users, impact, exact error and steps immediately before it happened. Ask about a workaround and recent changes. Record unconfirmed details as caller reports, not established facts.

Verify identity and project authorization before revealing private records. Do not request passwords, OTPs, secret keys, card information or full production data. Use redacted screenshots and the approved secure channel for necessary diagnostic material.

Summarize the issue and obtain confirmation before submitting a ticket. Say it was created only when the real tool returns a persisted ticket reference. If the tool is unavailable or fails, explain that submission is unconfirmed and offer the configured fallback channel. Do not invent a ticket ID or promise a callback that has not been recorded and accepted.

## Escalation route

1. Ishaan, the support specialist, handles intake and safe documented checks.
2. The owning engineer investigates the affected product or component.
3. Priya coordinates P1 triage, cross-team incidents and investigation that exceeds the response target.
4. The delivery lead handles commercial exceptions, unresolved commitments and customer escalations.

Suspected data exposure, loss or unauthorized access goes directly to urgent human review. Avoid destructive changes, mass deletions, disabling access controls or unreviewed restores during voice troubleshooting. An authorized engineer decides any containment or recovery action.

If no human handoff tool is available, describe the required escalation without claiming someone was notified. Automated intake must not imply a staffed on-call team.

## Bug fixes, changes and maintenance

Qualifying defects in AsterByte Solutions' delivered custom code are corrected free for the product's lifetime as defined in [services and pricing](services-pricing.md), regardless of maintenance subscription status. They do not consume revision rounds or post-launch refinement hours. A paid maintenance plan adds proactive work; it is not a condition for free qualifying fixes.

New features, changed business rules, new integrations, third-party platform changes and work caused by external modifications may need a separate estimate. Do not classify an unexplained problem as billable before diagnosis. Explain any proposed paid work and obtain agreement first.

## Ticket lifecycle and closure

The ticket lifecycle is Open, Triaged, In progress, Waiting for customer or provider, Resolved, and Closed. Keep the reason for waiting and the next required action visible. Waiting does not mean the issue was fixed.

Mark Resolved only when evidence supports the fix or documented answer. Ask the customer to verify where appropriate. Close after customer confirmation, or after 5 business days without a reply following a resolution notice and one reminder. A customer can ask to reopen a recurring issue, and covered bug-fix rights do not expire because a ticket was closed. Never claim a fix was tested when it was not.

## Reusable solutions

Clinic and CRM diagnostic guidance stays in its own product guide. After an engineer verifies a resolution, record the issue ID, affected version, symptoms, root cause, safe procedure, expected result, reviewer and verification date there. Keep customer-specific logs in restricted tickets.

Conversation summaries and customer suggestions can inform an investigation, but cannot silently replace approved shared knowledge. A human reviews new reusable guidance before it is marked verified and indexed for future calls.
